Record your weight on the Today tab: the chart appears after two entries. Weigh yourself in the morning, before breakfast.
Bars: the previous day\'s food against its target, green below it, red above. The dotted line is the target.
Sex, age, height and weight give your basal metabolic rate (Mifflin-St Jeor formula), activity gives your daily expenditure. The target is recalculated every time you record a new weight.
Desk work, almost no walking or exercise.
Exercise 3-5 times a week or a job on your feet.
Hard training 6-7 times a week or physical work.

Too little Pulsar data: the level is measured once %1$d days have passed since the first walk or workout. Until then the activity in the profile applies.
Over %1$d days walks and workouts added %2$d kcal a day on average, activity multiplier %3$s.

That is more than the activity in the profile (%1$s, %2$s), so the target uses the profile: heart rate formulas tend to overstate walking. Walks beyond that do not raise the target: what they burn speeds up the weight loss.
The target now comes from the weight trend.
Over %1$d days you ate %2$d kcal a day on average and the weight changed by %3$s kg a week: expenditure %4$d kcal a day. Expenditure without the trend: %5$d kcal.
Too few weigh-ins: %1$d of %2$d needed in the last %3$d days. Until then the expenditure comes from Pulsar or the activity in the profile.
The weigh-ins cover %1$d days, %2$d needed. Until then the expenditure comes from Pulsar or the activity in the profile.
The diary is filled for %1$d days between the weigh-ins, %2$d needed. Until then the expenditure comes from Pulsar or the activity in the profile.

Expenditure from the weight trend: what you ate plus what the weight lost (7700 kcal per kg) over the last 4 weeks. It needs a full diary and a weigh-in at least every few days, and then it takes the place of Pulsar and the activity in the profile. In the first weeks of a diet part of the loss is water, so the expenditure comes out high; days logged incompletely make it low. It only lowers the target, never raises it.
The trend is higher, so it is not used: it only lowers the target. Losing weight faster than the chosen pace does not raise the target.
Burned kcal are not added to today\'s target: they refine it through the two-week average.

Target = expenditure minus a deficit for the chosen pace (about 7700 kcal per kg of fat). For safety it is never below 1200 kcal for women and 1500 for men and not below your basal metabolic rate, and the pace is capped at 1 percent of body weight per week. The protein target helps keep muscle while losing weight.

This is an estimate from population formulas: the real expenditure differs from person to person by 10-20 percent. Judge by your weight over 2-3 weeks and adjust the target. The app is not a medical device. Not intended for pregnancy, breastfeeding, people under 18, eating disorders, diabetes and other conditions where diet should be agreed with a doctor.
Basal rate %1$d kcal, expenditure %2$d kcal, protein at least %3$d g
Expected loss: %1$s kg a week, goal in about %2$d weeks
Raised to the safe minimum: the loss will be slower than chosen.
Pace limited to 1 percent of weight a week.
Weight is below normal for your height: the target is for maintenance, no deficit.
Goal reached: the target is for maintaining weight.

Photos and text are recognized by the Claude Haiku 5.5 model. It is paid per use through Claude Console, separately from Claude subscriptions: about 0.05 cents per photo.

1. Sign in to Claude Console (button below).
2. Top up the balance in Billing.
3. Create a key in API keys and copy it.
4. Paste it here and press Save.

The key is stored on this phone only, encrypted, and is not copied to the cloud backup.
No API key: photo and text recognition are off.
The key was not accepted. Check that it was copied in full and has not been revoked.
Keys, balance and spending are managed on the Anthropic website.
The pages open in a built-in browser tab; you sign in with your Claude Console account. The balance cannot be read with a regular API key, so the app counts its own spending below.

Estimated from the tokens in each answer at the price of the model that answered. Claude Haiku 5.5 costs 10 cents per million input tokens and 50 cents per million output tokens. The exact amount is on the Usage page in Console.
Keys, usage and limits are managed on the Google website.
The pages open in a built-in browser tab; you sign in with your Google account. The Usage page shows how much of the free daily limit is used.

Counted by the app from the tokens in each answer, thinking included, at the paid tier prices (Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite: 30 cents per million input tokens and 2.50 dollars per million output tokens). On the free tier Google charges nothing, and the sum is shown as what it would cost. Google counts its daily limit from midnight Pacific time; the exact usage is on the Usage page in AI Studio.
On the paid tier it would be

Google does not tell the app which tier the key is on, so choose it here. A key becomes paid when billing is linked to its project in AI Studio: requests are then charged at the paid prices, and Google does not use what is sent to improve its products. The spending counter adds up paid prices either way; this choice only changes how the sum is shown and the privacy note.
The photo or text is sent to Google (Gemini) for recognition. Location and other photo metadata are removed before sending.

Gemini did not accept the API key. Check it in settings.
The photo or text is sent to Google (Gemini) for recognition. On the free tier Google may use it to improve its products. Location and other photo metadata are removed before sending.

Which model recognizes photos and text. If the chosen model is retired, the next one with a key answers instead, and the review screen says so. Gemini needs its own key from Google AI Studio: the free tier costs nothing, but Google may use what is sent.
%1$s answered \"not found\" on %2$s. Until it is back, the next one with a key answers.

Optional: a fallback or free recognizer.

1. Open Google AI Studio (button below) and sign in with a Google account.
2. Create an API key and copy it.
3. Press Add key, paste it and press Save.

The free tier needs no card. On it Google may use the photos and text sent to improve its products. The key is stored on this phone only, encrypted.

The backup holds the diary, the weight log, My dishes and the profile with the goal. The Claude key, saved Claude answers and unsent requests are not included. CSV is the diary only, for spreadsheets: it cannot be imported back.

Add: only records that are not on this phone yet are added, and the profile is taken from the file only if none is filled in here. Replace: the diary, weight log, dishes and profile become exactly as in the file.
